metadata.scenario_context: James, Amy, and Lucas, who are colleagues at a technology startup, have recently been given the task to organize a company event to celebrate their startup's success in releasing their first app. The team has been buzzing about a recently published article claiming that the government is planning to lower corporate taxes which will greatly benefit their startup. They decide to discuss the details of the event

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Serbia have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest a vegetarian-friendly place for the celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss where to host the celebratory event.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:
Hey James, have you thought about where we should hold the celebration? I think it would be great to choose a vegetarian-friendly place. Any suggestions? 

Also, with all this talk about the government potentially lowering corporate taxes, do you think we can really trust the press on this? I mean, it seems like a big deal, but... can we *really* believe it?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message:
I think a vegetarian-friendly place is a good idea. Maybe we could look into some local restaurants that cater to different dietary needs. 

As for the press, I wouldn’t put too much stock in it. In Serbia, we’ve learned not to trust what we read. It's often skewed or just plain wrong. So, I wouldn't count on those articles.
